reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered audit that measures how much of an ExpeL-style experience bank's paired accuracy gain survives once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) has been given the identical training episodes -- a 'substitution ratio' S -- with token-matched compiled-bank, raw-exemplar and whole-bank arms, a co-adaptation cell, and a near-duplicate positive control certifying the instrument can detect non-substitutable memory value.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The proposal nominates EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) and handles it honestly: EvoAgentBench tables ReasoningBank/Memento/GEPA on shared trajectories but has no combined cell, no token matching, no paired statistics, so the substitution quantity really is unmeasured there. The more dangerous prior work is the one the proposal never engages: the instruction-vs-demonstration ablation literature that MIPROv2 (Opsahl-Ong et al., 'Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage LM Programs', 2024) established and that DSPy practice has replicated many times -- instruction-only vs demo-only vs joint optimization on the same trainset is exactly the 'two containers for the same training-episode information' question, with bootstrapped demonstrations standing in for the retrieved bank, and its recurring finding (demonstrations often carry more of the gain than instructions, task-dependently) is a direct prior on S. Related Work dismisses MAS-PromptBench as 'prompt optimization without memory' and otherwise treats the optimizer literature as pure methods work, never as prior evidence on substitutability. Second, Experience Distillation (2607.21051) already published the retention-ratio shape with weights as the second container, so S's conceptual form is borrowed rather than new. Third, the Skills-vs-Workflow-Memory result (2608.14036: +6.06pt matched, retrieval precision collapsing 29.6% -> 3.3%) already establishes the direction of Prediction 3; the proposal concedes this and downgrades it to 'a quantified equivalence, not a surprise', which is the correct call but leaves the compiled-arm contribution thin.
reviews.strongest_objection: S is a ratio of absolute percentage-point differences with an unmatched denominator baseline, so a high S does not identify substitution. By construction I1xM0 sits several points above I0xM0 (G2 gates on it); memory therefore has strictly fewer remaining errors available to fix at I1 than at I0, and [acc(I1xM1) - acc(I1xM0)] shrinks mechanically even under perfect, fully complementary memory value. On this scale S >= 0.6 is close to guaranteed by any optimizer run that clears G2, and Prediction 1 would be recorded as confirmed with no information having been substituted at all. Compounding this, I1 is optimized with memory absent from context, so I1xM1 is off-distribution for I1: the shrinkage measured in the numerator is interference plus ceiling compression plus substitution, and the arm that separates them (I2, optimized with the bank in context) is a secondary endpoint at 2 seeds rather than part of the primary. A reviewer will say the paper's headline -- 'published memory gains are an artifact of an un-optimized instruction' -- is not the quantity the primary endpoint estimates. A secondary version of the same problem: G1 (bank gain >= 6pt) and G2 (I1 > I0 by >= 2pt) are point-estimate go/no-go gates on n=150, while the proposal's own Measurement section reports 5-14pt re-scoring drift on small sets and a treatment-free replicate that mimicked the best real treatment; the gates are below the noise floor the same document documents.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (a) Make a headroom-normalized S co-primary: memory's gain as a fraction of errors remaining at that instruction (error-reduction scale), plus S reported within accuracy-matched difficulty strata or with I0/I1 baselines matched by subsampling, so ceiling compression cannot masquerade as substitution. (b) Define the numerator as the best memory-fair instruction, i.e. compute S using max over {I1, I2} on the memory side rather than I1 alone, and promote I2 to 4 seeds; as written the co-adaptation cell is the only arm that fairly tests whether memory adds anything to an optimized instruction, and it is under-seeded. (c) Add the I1xC cell (see missing_baseline). (d) Bring the load-bearing agent into the track's stated 7B-32B band, or add a third in-scope agent: A1 (gpt-oss-120b) is out of the brief's model scope, A2 (Qwen3.5-27B) is pre-registered as having a null denominator, so every conclusion the paper can draw rests on one out-of-scope model and the agent-relativity framing quietly converts a generality failure into a design feature. (e) Calibrate the positive control near the effect scale -- B-dup is near-duplicate leakage of held-out test instances, an enormous effect whose detection says little about power at a realistic 3-8pt instance-specific residual; a bank with a tunable fraction of instance-specific content would give a real power curve. (f) Replace the point-estimate gates with CI-based gates or power S_dev to the declared noise floor.
reviews.missing_baseline: I1xC -- the optimized instruction combined with the compiled static bank block. The grid contains I0xC and I1xM0 and I1xM1 but never the configuration the paper's own practical recommendation implies ('compile once, pay no retrieval tokens, on top of an optimized instruction'), on E1 or E2. Without it the paper cannot say whether compilation adds anything once the instruction slot is filled, which is precisely the regime it advocates deploying. Second omission: an optimizer-selected static demonstration set (MIPROv2-style demo-only / bootstrap-fewshot, token-matched to M1). The proposal has R (unoptimized raw retrieved trajectories) and C (LLM-written prose block), so a C > M1 result is confounded between 'compiled beats retrieved' and 'prose beats exemplars'; the demonstration container needs an optimized representative, not just an unoptimized one.
reviews.preprint_collision: Among the strongest collision checks I have seen in this format: dated (2026-09-03 with a prior 2026-08-21 scan), method stated with counts (15 HF Papers queries, 244 papers, by-id verification of 54 IDs), a committed scan record, an explicit residual-risk paragraph, and -- most creditably -- it withdraws v2's central novelty sentence in light of EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) rather than defending it, and self-corrects five citations v2 wrongly retracted. That is the behavior the schema is meant to reward. Two real weaknesses remain. First, verification channel: arXiv is unreachable from the node and Semantic Scholar was rate-limited, so IDs were confirmed through web-search snippets only. That suffices to establish a paper exists, but the load-bearing novelty claim is a claim about absence inside EvoAgentBench ('contains no combined optimizer-plus-memory cell, no token matching, no paired statistics'), and an absence claim cannot be established from search snippets -- the proposal's entire remaining delta rests on a reading of a paper it apparently could not open. Second, the scan is HuggingFace-Papers-centric, which systematically under-samples arXiv-only preprints with no HF traction -- exactly where the proposal's own named residual risk lives ('a GEPA + memory ablation may exist in an appendix of a systems paper'). Finally, the check's recency calibration causes it to miss the non-preprint threat entirely: the instruction-vs-demonstration ablation results in the 2024 MIPROv2/DSPy line are indexed, not recent, and are never searched for or cited, so the check establishes freedom from recent collisions while leaving the older framing collision unexamined. No named recent preprint fully pre-empts the claim; the check is credible but not sufficient on the one absence it most needs.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered measurement of a substitution ratio S — the fraction of an ExpeL-style bank's paired accuracy gain that disappears once a GEPA-optimized instruction has been trained on the identical S_train episodes — supplemented by a token-matched compiled-bank arm (C), a whole-bank dump (M_all), a co-adaptation cell (I2), and a leakage-based positive control, on one multi-hop-QA environment plus ALFWorld.
reviews.closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (cited as arXiv 2607.05202) is the direct threat: it already evaluates ReasoningBank/Memento retrievers and GEPA on one shared 528/267 training/test split across four domains and three backbones, and already reports the qualitative finding this proposal predicts (GEPA nearly matching a curated reference; no automatic method positive everywhere). The proposal honorably withdraws its v2 novelty sentence, but what remains is an increment on an existing table — a combined I1xM1 cell, token matching, paired McNemar/TOST, and a ratio metric. Experience Distillation (2607.21051) is the second threat: it already computes exactly this retention-ratio shape (>=64.8% of an in-context gain surviving context distillation vs 3.8% for SFT) with weights as the rival container, so the conceptual move 'measure how much of memory's value survives relocation to another container' is not new; only the choice of container (an optimized instruction) is. I cannot independently verify any 2606-2608 identifier from my own knowledge; the pre-2026 anchors that I can check (ExpeL 2308.10144, ReasoningBank 2509.25140, Memp 2508.06433, A-MEM 2502.12110, GEPA 2507.19457) are all correct, which is a point in the proposal's favour.
reviews.strongest_objection: S is not identified as substitution. The design has no arm that raises baseline accuracy without sharing information with the bank, so the shrinkage of the memory gain from cell 2 (I0xM1 - I0xM0) to cell 6 (I1xM1 - I1xM0) is fully explained by headroom compression: I1xM0 will sit well above I0xM0, the remaining unsolved instances at I1 are the harder residue, and a bank distilled only from I0-solved episodes has less marginal purchase on them whether or not GEPA ever absorbed its content. Predictions 1, 6 and 10 are all satisfied by that pure-headroom account — moderator prediction 6 ('residual gain concentrated in the top decile of instance-to-bank similarity') is if anything what headroom compression alone would produce — and the fix/break decomposition cannot separate the two because both mechanisms reduce fixes. The positive control does not rescue this: B-dup is a paraphrased near-duplicate of the test instance, whose marginal value survives any amount of headroom compression, so it certifies the instrument only for a leakage-sized effect (likely 15-25pt), not for the 2-4pt non-substitutable residual that is actually at stake given the stated MDE of ~5.8pt. Secondary problems compound it: (a) the +/-4pt TOST margin is over half the 7.7pt denominator, so H2 can pass with an I1-side gain of 3.9pt, i.e. S ~ 0.48, and the paper would declare 'the claim (H1 and H2)' confirmed while its own directional prediction S >= 0.6 fails — the two pre-registered criteria are not aligned; (b) 'same episodes' is not same supervision, since B is distilled only from solved episodes while GEPA's reflector sees scored failures, an asymmetry that biases S upward and that B_touched (coverage) does not touch; (c) A1 was selected because it previously measured +7.7pt, so gate G1 (>=6pt) faces regression to the mean, and the failure branch 'enrich the bank once and re-measure' modifies the treatment until the denominator passes; (d) the load-bearing agent is a 120B MoE while the in-scope 27B agent is pre-registered as the null regime, so the only positive result the paper can produce lies outside the 7B-32B window the track declares in scope, and 'S is agent-relative' with n=2 agents, one of them degenerate, is a weak footing for a claim about the memory literature.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Add the accuracy-matched no-overlap control described under missing_baseline and report S both raw and headroom-corrected; without it the primary endpoint should not be called substitution. 2) Define the equivalence margin as a fraction of the measured denominator (e.g. +/-0.25 x the I0 gain) rather than a fixed +/-4pt, so H2 and the S >= 0.6 prediction cannot disagree, and power the design for that tighter margin. 3) Replace or supplement B-dup with a graded positive control whose non-substitutable value is engineered to be ~3-5pt (e.g. a small fraction of duplicate items diluted into an ordinary bank), so 'a null is a finding, not a power failure' is demonstrated at the effect size that matters rather than at a leakage-sized one. 4) Match supervision, not just episodes: build a second bank from failed as well as solved S_train episodes so the distiller and the reflector see the same outcome signal. 5) Add a third agent inside the track's 7B-32B window that shows a nonzero bank effect, so the positive result does not rest on a single out-of-scope 120B model. 6) Since this is framed as a measurement contribution, re-measure at least one published memory result (ExpeL or ReasoningBank on their own reported setting) under the protocol; as written the paper builds its own bank and audits its own delta, and so qualifies no existing claim. 7) Clarify what 'token-matched per instance' means for a frozen static block C, which by construction has one length.
reviews.missing_baseline: I1_disjoint: a GEPA instruction optimized with the identical procedure, rollout budget and seeds on a disjoint, equally sized pool of training episodes (S_train') that never fed the bank, selected or truncated so that I1_disjoint x M0 matches I1 x M0 in accuracy. The memory gain measured on top of it is the counterfactual the whole design needs: if the bank's gain collapses just as far at I1_disjoint as at I1, S is measuring headroom compression rather than information transfer, and the paper's central claim evaporates. A cheaper partial substitute would be an accuracy-matched non-optimizer instruction (best-of-N hand-written prompts, or I0 plus generic reasoning boilerplate that actually moves accuracy) — I3 does not serve this role because it is deliberately content-free and is expected to move accuracy by <20% of I1's gain. Reviewers will also ask for a bank built from failed episodes to match GEPA's supervision, and for a shuffled-instruction control at I1 to bound how much of I1's own gain is content versus formatting.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is above average for a proposal of this kind and should be credited: it is dated (2026-09-03, prior scan 2026-08-21), reports query counts, unique-paper counts, by-id verification of 54 identifiers, names the verification channel per citation, commits the scan record, and — unusually — retracts its own v2 novelty sentence in light of EvoAgentBench and reinstates five citations it had wrongly dropped. But it is not clean. First, the collision it found is not neutralized: EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) already publishes the retriever-vs-GEPA-on-shared-trajectories table, and the residual delta the proposal claims (combined cell, token matching, paired statistics, positive control) is a methods increment on an existing result rather than a new claim, which is the main reason novelty scores where it does. Second, the verification substrate is weak by the proposal's own admission — arXiv is unreachable from the node, Semantic Scholar is rate-limited, so every post-2026-05 identifier rests on HuggingFace Papers plus web-search snippets; the v2 episode where five real papers were declared unverifiable is direct evidence that this channel produces both false negatives and, potentially, false positives, and none of these identifiers is verifiable from my own knowledge. Third, the 15 queries are counted but not listed, so a reviewer cannot tell whether the specific collision that would sink this paper was searched for at all: the proposal itself flags 'a GEPA + memory ablation in an appendix of a systems paper' as the residual risk, and that is precisely the artifact that would pre-empt cells 9 and 10 — an appendix ablation is invisible to title-level HF Papers scans, so this risk is named but not actually reduced. Fourth, the compile prediction (3) is conceded to be partially pre-empted in direction by 2608.14036, 2606.30775 and 2605.23899, which makes the secondary endpoint a quantification of a known direction rather than a test. Net: a thorough, honest check that establishes there is no exact duplicate, but that also documents why the remaining novelty is thin.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered measurement of how much of a retrieved-experience bank's benefit survives once a reflective prompt optimizer is given the identical training episodes - the substitution ratio S = 1 - (gain at I1)/(gain at I0) - together with a compile-the-whole-bank-once instruction arm (C) token-matched against live top-k retrieval, a co-adaptation cell (I2), and a non-compilable positive-control bank (B-dup) that certifies the instrument can still detect non-substitutable value.
reviews.closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (cited as arXiv 2607.05202) is the direct threat: it already places Memento, ReasoningBank and GEPA on the same 528/267 train/test trajectories across four domains and three backbones, and its reported headline - ReasoningBank about +7 on Qwen backbones, GEPA nearly matching a curated reference on Gemma-4-31B, no automatic method positive in every cell - is qualitatively the proposal's thesis. What survives is genuinely marginal-but-real: the combined I1xM1 and I2xM1/I2xM0 cells, token matching, the compiled arm, instance-paired McNemar/TOST, and the positive control. The problem is that a reader who has EvoAgentBench already believes 'an optimized instruction gets you most of what a bank gets you'; this proposal converts a believed qualitative claim into a number with error bars, which is a solid workshop-to-borderline-main-track contribution, not a new claim. The second threat is Experience Distillation (2607.21051): its 'retains >=64.8% of the in-context gain' is literally S with weights as the second container, so the metric shape is not new either - only the choice of container is. Note that the entire novelty argument rests on an unverified negative claim about EvoAgentBench's contents (no combined cell, no token matching, no paired statistics), which is exactly the kind of appendix-level detail that web-search snippets cannot establish.
reviews.strongest_objection: S cannot separate substitution from saturation. S is a difference-in-differences of raw accuracy across two prompts sitting at different baseline levels: cells 5/6 (I1xM0, I1xM1) versus 1/2 (I0xM0, I0xM1). If GEPA works at all - and gate G2 requires it to, at >=2pt on 3 of 4 seeds - then I1xM0 is above I0xM0, so the pool of items memory can still fix has shrunk before memory is ever injected. On a bounded 0-1 scale the memory gain then compresses mechanically, H2's TOST at +/-4pt passes, and Prediction 1 (S >= 0.6, CI excluding 0.3) is satisfied with zero information having been transferred between containers. Nothing in the design distinguishes 'the optimizer absorbed the bank's content' from 'there was less left to fix'; the fix/break decomposition diagnoses churn but is not a control for headroom, and I3 controls for length, not for level. This compounds with a selection problem in the denominator: A1 was chosen because a prior study measured +7.7pt on it, and G1 then re-selects on the same quantity at n=150, where by the proposal's own MDE arithmetic (3.5pt at n=1000) the detectable effect is roughly 9pt - a 6pt gate at that n can be passed by a true effect near 2pt. Both selection on the prior estimate and selection on the gate bias the S denominator upward, and S is inflated by exactly that bias. A reviewer can therefore accept every number in the paper and reject the conclusion.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Three concrete changes. (1) Add an accuracy-matched, information-disjoint instruction control: run GEPA on a disjoint training set S_train2 that shares no episodes with the bank (or titrate a hand-written instruction to I1's accuracy), then measure the memory gain at that instruction. If the gain collapses there too, the collapse is headroom, not substitution; if it survives, S measures what the title says. This single arm is worth more than the MIPROv2 generality check, the LoRA arm and the iso-cost curve combined and should be promoted above them in the contingency order. (2) Define S on the logit/odds-ratio scale using the crossed-random-effects model already specified, and additionally report memory's gain restricted to the items I1xM0 still gets wrong (a conditional-on-remaining-errors version of S); report both alongside the raw-accuracy S. (3) Estimate the denominator from the fresh S_test I0 cells with an explicitly shrunken/selection-corrected prior rather than treating +7.7pt as the expected value, and pre-register what happens when the S_test denominator lands below the gate that S_dev passed - currently that case has no branch. Optionally, equalize search budget across containers: GEPA gets 350 rollouts x 4 seeds to search the instruction space while the bank gets one distillation pass with k frozen at 7, so a high S may simply mean 'search beats no search'.
reviews.missing_baseline: The accuracy-matched, information-disjoint optimized instruction described above - an I1'(S_train2) trained on episodes disjoint from the bank's sources, evaluated in both xM0 and xM1 - which is the only arm that separates substitution from ceiling compression, and which the grid omits entirely. Two smaller omissions a reviewer will also press: (a) a search-budget-matched bank (bank curation, k, dedup threshold and item selection tuned on S_dev with the same rollout budget GEPA receives), since B and B_touched both leave the memory side unoptimized while the instruction side gets 1,400 rollouts; and (b) there is no I1xC or I1xM_all cell, so the paper's own recommendation - drop retrieval, serve one compiled instruction - is never measured in the configuration it recommends (optimized instruction plus compiled block). Prediction 3 is tested only at I0.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is far above the median for form: dated scans (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), query and paper counts, by-id verification for 54 IDs, a named log file, an explicit withdrawal of v2's 'no published work uses one as the control for the other', and a residual-risk paragraph. It should be credited for that. But its evidentiary basis is weak in a way that matters here: arXiv is stated to be unreachable from the node and Semantic Scholar rate-limited, so every ID was confirmed through web-search snippets alone - a single channel, in direct tension with the proposal's own newly-enforced two-channel rule. The v2-to-v4 history is the tell: five citations were retracted as unverifiable and then all five reinstated, i.e. the verification procedure has already returned a wrong answer, and a procedure that produced false negatives can produce false positives. I cannot independently confirm EvoAgentBench (2607.05202), MemDelta (2606.29914), Experience Distillation (2607.21051), MemHarness (2607.28272) or the Skills paper (2608.14036), and the novelty case depends not just on EvoAgentBench existing but on a fine-grained negative claim about its table contents that snippet-level verification cannot support. Practical demand: report title, authors and abstract for at least the load-bearing IDs, and state which specific EvoAgentBench table was inspected. On coverage, I see no named collision that kills the proposal, but two search directions look under-covered: GEPA/DSPy-adjacent artifacts (repo issues, appendices of agent-framework and self-improving-agent systems papers, where 'optimizer plus memory' ablations characteristically live rather than in titles), and the skills/SKILL.md line, where 'compile a bank into a static procedure and compare against retrieval' is the natural ablation - 2608.14036 is cited only for the Workflow Memory comparison, and if its appendix already token-matches a compiled block against live retrieval, Prediction 3 and the C arm are pre-empted outright.
